SUMMARYThe Program Therapist is responsible for direct therapeutic services to children and their parents/caregivers. Counseling sessions may be held at the client’s school, home, or at the office, according to the client’s and parent/guardian’s preference. Collaborates with attending psychiatrist who provides client’s medication management. Collaborates with the United Women of East Africa Support Team to ensure effective service delivery, community engagement, and alignment with organizational objectives Collaborates with schools via IEP’s and monthly contacts with teachers, counselors and other school support team members. Fosters ongoing working relationships with school and community members. Collaborates with community resources to support clients and provide referrals for services outside our program’s scope. May receive training in Parent Child Interactive Therapy (PCIT), an evidence-based model for treating 2–7-year-olds. Attends staff meetings weekly and participates in professional supervision in line with BBS standards. Meets all clinical documentation standards of the program, agency, and clinical field. Adheres to all agency policies, including productivity targets and documentation requirements. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIESWork collaboratively with the United Women of East Africa Support Team to ensure effective service delivery, community engagement, and alignment with organizational objectives.Is familiar with the principles of System of Care, and the Wraparound Philosophy. This is exemplified by interventions that are based on the strengths and needs of the child, youth, and family. Treatment will be individualized, culturally appropriate to the family system, and inclusive of all important individuals to the child/family that represent natural or indigenous supports from the home, school, and/or community. Client and family input is regularly solicited and integrated into services, regarding the quality & outcome of services, development of treatment goals, and overall service delivery.Is familiar with the vision and mission of SDCC-ECOP.Seeks and utilizes outcome measures, in addition to client/family/Tx team feedback, as a means of measuring treatment progress and success. Regardless of a therapist’s theoretical orientation, there is accountability to service results as evidenced by the realistic goals of behavioral change on the part of the child, youth, and/or significant adults in the life of the child or youth.Responsible for comprehensive, clinically sound, efficient, and timely documentation and billing. Participates in ongoing training and Quality Assurance chart reviews to ensure the soundness of all client health records.Actively works toward providing timely services to clients and to meeting monthly and annual productivity targets.Incorporation of the program into family context through regular parent and staff communication. Promote positive program identity within SDCC-ECOP and the San Diego community at large.Collaborates with a multidisciplinary team at the outpatient clinic. Collaborates with school personnel in order to foster a collaborative working relationship and ensure quality service for clients. Efforts may include participation in IEPs and/or other school meetings, communication regarding referral status, and assistance needed to provide comprehensive quality care to client/family. Attendance at community events and/or collaborative meetings, as needed. Collaboration and case management with external treatment providers (i.e. TBS, wraparound, health services, substance use, recreational facilities, etc.).Participates in SDCC committee representation as assigned, on a rotating basis.Sets annual SMART goals and participates in regular performance reviews.Maintains a positive attitude and collaborative teamwork approach. Demonstrates respect for coworkers, clients, and office workspace/materials.Participates in training made available at SDCC-ECOP and in the community, as agreed upon with the Program Manager. Provides in-service training at SDCC-ECOP as agreed upon with Program Manager and/or Clinical Supervisor.Fulfills contract expectations of a 40-hour work week, or part-time hours per employee contract. Is available for sessions until 6pm 2-3 days a week. Is available to provide school and home based services, as well as attend meetings in the schools/community. Fulfills all paperwork requirements, including completing a weekly schedule and monthly statistics promptly.Participates in SDCC committee representation as assigned, on a rotating basis.Utilization of electronic records (Smart Care) established by The County of San Diego and continuously adheres to training requirements.Completion of a 10-hour online Trauma Focused-Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TFCBT) training. Completion of all required trainings by our county contract.Communicates directly to the Manager/Supervisor if any concerns or training needs are required in order to fulfill job expectations.Other duties as assigned by Program Manager and/or Clinical Supervisor. PERFORMANCE TARGETS:Meets minimum monthly productivity target of 60 hours based on a standard 40-hour workweek. Productivity expectations will be adjusted proportionate to hours worked.Productivity expectation allows for 6 weeks/year of time off per FTE for holiday, sick, vacation, trainings, etc. Will demonstrate a 90% customer satisfaction rating on customer satisfaction surveys.Will maintain an average of less than two chart errors per chart on internal audits. For purposes of this goal, an error shall be defined as an omission that would trigger a clear disallowance.Identifies an area of interest, and takes at least one training per year in this area, and presents new learning to the team. LANGUAGE SKILLS Ability to read, analyze, and interpret medical records, journals, reports, and legal documents; Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community; Ability to effectively present information to management and public groups REASONING ABILITY Ability to read, analyze, and interpret medical records, journals, reports, and legal documents; Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community; Ability to effectively present information to management and public groups PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand; walk; sit; use hand to finger; or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. Due to the emotional instability of the clients the employee may be subjected to kicking, hitting, punching, biting, hair pulling, etc. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. WORK ENVIRONMENT The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to outside weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Most services will be provided in or near the homes of the families we serve. Employees are considered essential service providers and will be expected to work with families in need during pandemics or natural disasters. DIVERSITY STATEMENT The San Diego Center for Children is committed to: Actively recruiting, retaining, and supporting diverse staff at all levels of the organization.Ensuring that diverse perspectives are included in the development and implementation of policies, practices and services, and that individuals feel empowered to advance our mission within an atmosphere of trust, safety, and respect.Encourage and provide access to professional development in order to deliver equitable and culturally informed services to the population we serve. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:Bilingual in Amharic, Somali, Swahili, and/or TigrinyaMaster's degree (M.A); in social work, psychology, education or related health services or equivalent educationRegistered Associate or Intern BBS number requiredDemonstrated experience in work with children, teenagers, and familiesAvailable to provide early evening appointments, at least 2x per week Valid Clinical License or Registration within the State of CaliforniaValid California Driver’s License (CDL)PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:Bilingual in Spanish or other languages represented in the service communityCardiopulmonary Resuscitation Certificate (CPR)Standard First AidCertification in Evidence Based Treatment Models (PCIT, EMDR, MI, etc)

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIESIn support of the client’s treatment plan and the wraparound plan of care, provide education, advocacy, crisis intervention, case management, rehabilitation, and other therapeutic services in a community-based fashion as they navigate through the systems of care Utilizes supervision, consultation, and training to provide high quality services to families, including evidence-based parenting curriculum and high fidelity wraparound Locate, coordinate and develop linguistically and culturally diverse informal and formal resources and networks for families in the communities where they reside Appropriately share personal story to enhance engagement with families and increase awareness of clinical staff about parenting challenges and difficulties maneuvering the ‘systems’, and maintain appropriate professional boundaries with families Provides culturally competent education and hands-on coaching to parents to help them better understand how the “systems” work, and the process of accessing community resources in their area Triage crisis situations with team members, including doing basic risk assessments, safety planning, and connecting to resources to maintain safety in the home, school, and community Assists parents in connection to needed behavioral health services Coordinates treatment with referring parties and outside resources including schools, psychiatrists, support groups, child care, government assistance, family advocacy programs, and others as appropriate. Participates in child and family team meetingsMaintains accurate, timely, and complete case records per Medi-Cal requirements and SDCC policies and procedures Maintains clear, effective, and open communication between multi-disciplinary clinical staff, and administrative personnel within and between SDCC programs Encourage involvement of parents in our Program Advisory Group (PAG) and WrapWorks events Availability to work several evenings a week Fulfills all required/assigned training including training in high fidelity wraparound, roadmap trainings, SDCC Partners Training, applicable EBP trainings, cultural competency, and HIPAA Maintains certified peer support specialist certification, if applicableAll other duties as assigned LANGUAGE SKILLS Ability to read, analyze, and interpret medical records, journals, reports, and legal documents; Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community; Ability to effectively present information to management and public groups.REASONING ABILITY Ability to read, analyze, and interpret medical records, journals, reports, and legal documents; Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community; Ability to effectively present information to management and public group.PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Due to the emotional instability of the clients the employee may be subjected to kicking, hitting, punching, biting, hair pulling, etc. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. WORK ENVIRONMENT The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to outside weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Most services will be provided in or near the homes of the families we serve. Employees are considered essential service providers and will be expected to work with families in need during pandemics or natural disasters. DIVERSITY STATEMENT The San Diego Center for Children is committed to: Actively recruiting, retaining, and supporting diverse staff at all levels of the organization.Ensuring that diverse perspectives are included in the development and implementation of policies, practices and services, and that individuals feel empowered to advance our mission within an atmosphere of trust, safety, and respect.Encourage and provide access to professional development in order to deliver equitable and culturally informed services to the population we serve. jobs.description: Employer: Lane County Government - Health & Human Services Expires: 11/20/2026 About the PositionLane County Behavioral Health is looking for dynamic Qualified Mental Health Associates to join our team as mobile crisis service responders for our new Mobile Crisis Service of Lane County program (MCS) which was created to better serve individuals in behavioral health crisis across our county.These positions will work in two-person teams to respond to calls for service in rural and metro areas of Lane County. Duties will include providing phone-based, office-based, and community-based crisis assessment, intervention, and safety planning services to individuals experiencing behavioral health crises, using standardized tools and strategies following training, with oversight from and access to back-up support from behavioral health clinical staff. These positions will also provide follow-up referrals and case management support to individuals served following a behavioral health crisis. Lane County Behavioral Health is looking for dedicated individuals who are focused on solutions, with a passion to serve and who are driven to connect. These positions do require a QMHA Certification through MHACBO. About the DivisionLane County Behavioral Health provides services to more than 1,600 individuals with behavioral health conditions. We work with community partners to provide a continuum of care from prevention through treatment and aftercare in an environment that promotes a culture of resilience and recovery.*Lane County employees may be eligible for student loan repayment: See links below.Public Service Loan ForgivenessNational Health Service Corps Find out from Lane County employees how it is to work for the Behavioral Health division.Schedule: Schedule will be four - 10-hour shifts Wednesday - Saturday 2:00 p.m. - 12:00 a.m. The initial training will include three weeks of training 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. This program may include overtime, and/or non-traditional work hours, including nights and weekends, and some holidays. These positions include community-based work and related travel for routine job tasks. *This is an AFSCME represented position* QUALIFICATIONS:Training: Bachelor's degree in a behavioral science field from an accredited university with major course work in a mental health field, psychology, sociology or a related field.OR:Experience: At least one year of work experience working directly with mentally or emotionally disturbed clients, and a combination of education, training and/or work experience in a behavioral sciences field that totals two additional years, plus the required competencies.OR:A combination of at least three year's relevant work, education, training or experience, AND have the competencies necessary to a) communicate effectively, b) understand mental health assessment treatment and service terminology and to apply the concepts, and c) provide psychosocial skills development and to implement interventions prescribed on a treatment plan within their scope of practice, is qualifying.Special Requirements:QMHA Certification through MHACBONPITranscriptsDiplomaCV or ResumeDRIVER’S LICENSE:Must be in possession of a valid driver's license at time of application, and a valid Oregon Driver's license by time of appointment.Notes:Successfully passing the ODHS ORCHARDS background check is required for this position. Successfully passing a mandatory CJIS FBI fingerprint-based background check is required for this position.Offers of employment are contingent upon consenting to, and successfully passing, a drug screening test.Please note that as part of the screening process Lane County will verify license and certification status. Studies have shown that women and BIPOC individuals are less likely to apply for jobs unless they believe they are able to perform every task in the job description. We are most interested in finding the best candidate for the job, and that candidate may be one who comes from a less traditional background. The county will consider any equivalent combination of knowledge, skills, education, and experience to meet minimum qualifications. If you are interested in applying, we encourage you to think broadly about your background and skill set for the role. CLASSIFICATION DETAILS:Mental Health Associate (Download PDF reader) SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATIONSelection ProcessEqual Employment OpportunityLane County is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diversity, equity, and inclusion as essential elements that create and foster a welcoming workplace. All qualified persons will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, political affiliation, disability or any other factor unrelated to the essential functions of the job.Strategic PlanIn alignment with Lane County's Strategic Plan, incumbent(s) will be expected to demonstrate the following core behaviors: Passion to Serve, Driven to Connect, and Focused on Solutions.The 2025 - 2027 Strategic Plan (Download PDF reader) focuses on the areas that Lane County will pursue as a way to deliver on our vision for the residents of Lane County. To meet these challenges, we know that the basis of our efforts lies in leveraging our people and partnerships to achieve our Strategic Priorities. We also recognize that the quality and commitment of our staff is essential to a shared future where Lane County is the best place in which to live, work, and play.Veteran Preference InformationTrauma Informed Care StatementLane County Health & Human Services is committed to providing Trauma Informed Care. As an organization, we recognize that many of the people we serve have experienced trauma, either currently, recently or in their past. Our agency is dedicated to incorporating an understanding of trauma, both with our clients and with each other. Our employees receive ongoing training to develop or deepen their understanding of trauma and its impacts.

jobs.description: Employer: Seriously Addictive Mathematics - USA Expires: 11/20/2026 S.A.M, or Seriously Addictive Mathematics, is a Mathematics Learning Program from Singapore, with a unique Mathematics curriculum designed for students from 4 to 12 years of age. Our curriculum is modelled after the Singapore Math method/pedagogy, which is one of the most successful and internationally recognised, according to the global TIMSS (Trends in International Maths & Science Study) survey. Topics covered in our program are relevant to all school going children in the US. Many public school districts, private schools and homeschoolers use the Singapore Math curriculum.We are looking for Center Supervisors and Math Instructors to join our team at our Los Altos (CA) location for the school year of 2026-27.This is a part-time position which can range from 10-30 hours/week. Center opening hours are generally 1.30pm-6.30pm weekdays and Saturdays/Sundays 8.30am-12.00pmOur Math instructors are mentors who will teach kids using our curriculum in a small group (3-4 kids) setting. jobs.description: Employer: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI) Expires: 11/20/2026 The Oregon Museum of Science & Industry (OMSI) is currently seeking Outdoor Science Instructors to join our Camp Gray team at the Coastal Discovery Center located in Newport, Oregon. This position is a part of a passionate team of educators and learners committed to providing transformative concept-based outdoor science education experiences. Using OMSI curricula, instructors plan and lead lessons that are student-centered and place-based for all ages. jobs.description: Employer: Simi Valley Unified School District Expires: 11/20/2026 PURPOSE: To establish an eligibility list for part-time vacancies and substitute assignments during the 10-month school year. The eligibility list will remain active for six months. The current vacancy is a part-time, 10-month position (6 hours/day).APPLICATION DEADLINE: Applications are submitted no later than 11:59 pm. on December 10, 2027. Apply here: https://www.schooljobs.com/careers/simivalleyusd/jobs/3386971/paraeducator-deaf-or-hard-of-hearing?keywords=paraeducator%20deaf&pagetype=jobOpportunitiesJobsTESTING PROCESS:A) Multiple Choice Test = 40% weighting on final scoreTentatively scheduled for as early as the week of December 14, 2026B) Structured Interview = 60% weighting on final scoreTentatively scheduled for as early as the week of January 4, 2027Applicants will be tested on English - Language Arts, Math and Ability to Assist in Instruction as well as ability to Interpret and communicate fluently using ASL sign language system.Applicants must meet the minimum qualifications stated in the job posting by the application deadline in order to move forward in the testing process. Those candidates who meet the minimum qualifications will be invited to the multiple choice test. Those with the highest scores on the multiple choice test will be invited to the structured interview. The testing process is subject to change as needs dictate. All communication regarding this process will be delivered via email.The information included in the Work Experience section of the application will determine whether applicants meet minimum qualifications. Please make sure you include ALL current and previous employment in the Work Experience section of the application and complete ALL fields.Class specifications are intended to present a descriptive list of the range of duties performed by employees in the class. Specifications are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job.Purpose StatementUnder the direct supervision of a certificated teacher and/or program administrator, the Paraeducator, Deaf or Hard of Hearing (DHH) assists students who are deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, and/or deaf or hard of hearing with multiple disabilities in specialized educational and postsecondary transition programs, including programs serving students ages 18–22.The Paraeducator provides instructional and communication support on a one-to-one or group basis by reinforcing lesson plans, facilitating access to instruction, and supporting student communication using American Sign Language (ASL), tactile communication strategies, Assistive Technology devices, and other evidence-based communication methods as identified in each student’s Individualized Education Program (IEP) or Individualized Transition Plan (ITP).The position supports student learning and independence by adapting instructional approaches to meet individual sensory, communication, cognitive, physical, and behavioral needs; maintaining instructional and behavioral records; and fostering communication, self-advocacy, and functional life skills consistent with IEP and postsecondary transition goals.Distinguishing Career FeaturesThe Paraeducator, Deaf or Hard of Hearing is distinguished from the general Paraeducator classification by its requirement for proficiency in American Sign Language (ASL) and knowledge of deaf culture, communication systems, and assistive technology used with deaf and hard of hearing students. Positions in this classification may serve students across preschool, K–12, and postsecondary transition (ages 18–22) programs, including community-based instruction and vocational settings. Unlike a credentialed Educational Interpreter, this classification does not require RID certification and does not function in an interpreting capacity; rather, incumbents assist in facilitating foster students in the development of communication skills and support IEP-driven instruction under the direction of the classroom teacher. Positions in this class may be assigned to salary range 65 or 70 based on educational attainment as described under Education and Experience.ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:Essential FunctionsInstructional Support Observes teacher lesson presentations and works with deaf or hard of hearing, deafblind, and DHH students with multiple disabilities to reinforce instruction by adjusting methods, pacing, and materials to individual student needs, alertness, sensory access, and learning conditions. Assists deaf or hard of hearing students on a one-to-one or group basis with academic subjects and study activities related to their Individualized Education Program (IEP).Motivates students by providing individual assistance and direction regarding assignments; supports students in completing assigned work.Supports instruction in life skills, employability skills, community access, and independent living activities for students ages 18–22 enrolled in postsecondary transition programs.Assists students in developing communication skills including American Sign Language (ASL), speech reading, and English language development.Uses both oral and manual communication, including facial expressions and physical gestures, to explain assignments and answer student questions.Assists deaf or hard of hearing students in becoming self-reliant in their communication and learning.May sign and read lessons aloud to students as directed by the supervising teacher.May assist deaf or hard of hearing students in a computer lab under the technical supervision of a teacher.May assist non- and limited-English-speaking students with language development skills.Communication Facilitation Facilitates communication between deaf or hard of hearing, deafblind, and/or DHH students with multiple disabilities and teachers, related service providers, employers, and school staff using ASL, tactile signing, object communication systems, PECS, Assistive Technology, listen to spoken language strategies, or other district-approved methods. Supports access to communication in school, community, and work-based learning settings for postsecondary transition students.Assists in facilitating the use of specialized communication and assistive technology equipment including visual tech devices and audio-visual equipment to support student learning.Assists primarily deaf or hard of hearing students in the utilization of classroom materials and equipment.Assists students with the daily operation and basic troubleshooting of personal hearing technology as directed by the teacher or audiologist.May help facilitate communication between deaf or hard of hearing students and Career Vocational Assistants for the purpose of job placement.Deaf Culture and Community Promotes and affirms Deaf identity, culture, and history in educational contexts, contributing to an inclusive and culturally affirming learning environment for deaf and hard of hearing students.Participates in programs, events, and instructional activities designed to foster Deaf Culture and Community, including Deaf awareness events, student groups, extracurricular activities, transition programming, and family engagement activities as assigned.Facilitates peer interaction and supports communication access between deaf or hard of hearing students and hearing peers and staff within the school community.Models respectful and affirming communication practices consistent with the diverse communication identities and preferences of deaf and hard of hearing studentsStudent Supervision and Behavior Support Monitors and supervises students in classroom settings, on the playground, in the bathroom, and other assigned areas to maintain safety and appropriate behavior.Applies behavior modification techniques and positive reinforcement strategies to maintain student control and a productive learning environment, consistent with behavior plans established by the certificated teacher or specialist.Implements student Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs) and de-escalation techniques as directed by the supervising teacher or behavioral specialist; documents behavioral data as required.Confers with teachers regarding individual student educational levels, specific learning needs, learning programs, and rate of progress.Serves as liaison between classroom teachers, designated instructional service providers, and resource specialists.Student Care and Physical Assistance Assists students in learning self-care skills including bathroom skills and eating skills.Moves students from area to area by foot or wheelchair as needed.Assists with lifting students in and out of wheelchairs, braces, and other orthopedic equipment.Assists students with toileting needs, including lifting the student to and from the toilet, managing clothing, washing hands, wiping, and changing diapers as required.Administers routine first aid and CPR to students as needed; maintains current certification.May hand-feed students who are unable to feed themselves.May ride on school bus with students and assist in the loading and unloading of students from buses and the transfer of students to and from classrooms.Record Keeping and Classroom Support Maintains daily records of instructional time spent with individual students and material covered.Administers a variety of modified tests as directed by the teacher and records results.Collects and records data on student performance, behavior, and communication progress for IEP goal monitoring as directed by the supervising teacher or specialist.Maintains a variety of student and classroom records as assigned.Assists in maintaining a neat, orderly, and supportive learning environment.May operate a variety of office equipment including copiers and computers.May travel to multiple classrooms or school sites to work with assigned students.Other Functions Performs other duties as assigned that support the overall objective of the positionMINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:Education and ExperienceEducation: Graduation from high school or equivalent (GED) is required.Experience: At least six months of experience utilizing American Sign Language to communicate with deaf or hard of hearing children or youth in a school, health services, or other structured environment is required. Experience working with special education students is desirable.Preferred Completion of 48 semester units or 72 quarter units of college coursework, or an Associate's degree or higher from an accredited college or university, is preferred and qualifies the incumbent for assignment at salary range 70.Licenses and Certificates May require a valid California Driver's License.Current CPR/First Aid certification required (or ability to obtain within six months of hire).SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION:Skills to: Operate a variety of educational and assistive technology equipment, including visual tech devices, computers, copiers, and specialized communication equipment used in special education programs.Utilize American Sign Language and manual communication with sufficient proficiency to assist deaf or hard of hearing students in communication skill development.Assist students with the operation and basic troubleshooting of personal hearing technology (hearing aids, cochlear implant processors, FM/DM systems) as directed.Implement behavior modification strategies and positive reinforcement techniques effectively.Apply basic instructional support techniques, including adapting materials and adjusting approaches to meet individual student needs.Knowledge of: American Sign Language (ASL) systems and basic manual communication skills.Multiple communication modalities used in DHH education, including ASL, Signed Exact English (SEE), Pidgin Signed English (PSE), and oral/aural approaches.Deafness, hearing loss, and foundational concepts of deaf culture.Deaf identity, Deaf community, and communication access rights as they apply to educational settings.English usage, grammar, spelling, and punctuation.Behavior modification techniques and positive/negative reinforcement systems.Principles of child guidance and student supervision techniques.Instructional methods and curriculum in grades Pre-K through post-secondary.Basic subjects taught in District schools.Principles of good public relations; interpersonal skills using tact, patience, and courtesy.Routine record-keeping techniques and data input and retrieval procedures.Classroom management techniques.Ability to: Communicate fluently using ASL and manual communication to assist deaf or hard of hearing students in accordance with their individual communication needs and IEP goals.Use total communication approaches including facial expressions and physical gestures to communicate effectively with deaf or hard of hearing students.Assess and adjust to students' language abilities and preferred communication methods.Demonstrate sensitivity to the communication needs of deaf or hard of hearing students.Establish rapport with and motivate students with diverse learning and communication needs.Establish and maintain effective working relationships with administrators, certificated staff, classified staff, parents, students, and the public.Exercise good judgment, maintain student discipline, and manage classroom situations effectively.Learn and apply instructional programs, curriculum, methods, and procedures as directed.Plan, organize, and prioritize work effectively within established time schedules.Communicate effectively both orally and in writing using correct English grammar, spelling, punctuation, and sentence structure.Understand and follow oral and written instructions.Analyze situations and adopt an effective course of action.Maintain confidentiality of student records and information in accordance with FERPA and district policy.Working EnvironmentPhysical Abilities: Stand and walk for extended periods in classroom and outdoor settings.Repetitively use fingers; use both hands simultaneously.Stoop, bend, reach overhead, and demonstrate rapid muscular coordination.Lift and carry up to 50 pounds; lift over 50 pounds with assistance.Push and pull students of varying weights in wheelchairs.Speak clearly and hear normal voice conversation.See and visually track individuals communicating in sign language.Use a computer, telephone, and other audio-visual equipment.Demonstrate hearing acuity sufficient to support communication facilitation in a variety of educational environments.Individuals protected by the Americans with Disability Act (ADA) may request accommodation if needed. In order for appropriate arrangements to be made for testing, your request must be received at the time your application is submitted. If special arrangements are not requested at the time the application is submitted, it is understood that no special accommodations are required. Documentation on the need for accommodation must accompany your request.Equal Employment Opportunity StatementThe Simi Valley Unified School District is committed to providing equal opportunity for all applicants for employment. The application, examination, and selection process shall be free from unlawful discrimination, including discrimination against an individual or group based on race, color, ancestry, nationality, national origin, ethnic group identification, age, religion, marital, pregnancy, or parental status, physical or mental disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, or genetic information; a perception of one or more of such characteristics; or association with a person or group with one or more of these actual or perceived characteristics.
